what: Why Dolby's decoder refuses one configuration 0 stream and accepts another: a control pair, and every field that fails to separate them

pair.refused: Snatch, a hybrid disc remux: Dolby writes six channels, mask 0x0c0f
pair.accepted: Dredd: Dolby writes sixteen object channels, and our objects agree to 52,44 dB

both: E-AC-3, acmod 7 + LFE, 768 kbit/s, no dependent substream, joc_dmx_config_idx 0, 15 JOC objects, 16 OAMD objects, one EMDF container per frame

fields_that_do_not_separate_them.frame and programme: acmod, lfeon, bit rate, channel list, chanmap, substream layout, CRC and tail counters -- identical
fields_that_do_not_separate_them.emdf container: version 0, key_id 0, four payloads with ids 1, 2, 11 and 14 -- identical
fields_that_do_not_separate_them.payload configuration: sample offset, duration, group id, discard_unknown_payload, payload_frame_aligned and create_duplicate, per payload -- identical
fields_that_do_not_separate_them.small payloads: payload 2 is 04 94 80 in both. Payload 1 is 02 00 in Snatch and 02 69 80 in Dredd, but Disclosure -- a configuration 3 stream Dolby accepts -- has the two-byte form 03 00, so the length is not the discriminator
fields_that_do_not_separate_them.oamd: 16 objects, bed at the same position, same gain and size, same block structure
fields_that_do_not_separate_them.joc header: same configuration, object count, band count, quantisation and slope distribution
fields_that_do_not_separate_them.sequence counter: Snatch has 48 zeros, but all 48 are its first 48 frames and a mid-file cut of the same title has none at all -- and Dolby refuses that cut too, so the zeros are not the cause

what_this_changes: the refusal is not about the configuration: a second stream at configuration 0 is accepted
it is not about the sequence counter, which the earlier work had already doubted and which a mid-file cut now rules out directly
the question is now properly posed, with a control that differs in nothing this decoder can read. What is left is a field oadec does not parse, or a decision the decoder takes on content
instrument_note: the obvious next experiment -- change one field of Snatch and see whether the refusal moves -- is not available: Dolby discards any EMDF payload rewritten in place. See payload-rewrite-rejected.json

the_content_is_not_it.why: the field-by-field difference found nothing and the mutation instrument is unavailable, because Dolby discards any payload rewritten in place. What is still available is the question the TrueHD titles answered: decode the refused stream's own objects, hand them back to Dolby's encoder, and ask Dolby again
the_content_is_not_it.method: `decode --format damf --no-bed-conform`, then `dee encode_to_atmos_ddp` from that set at 768 kbit/s, then the same object-mode command that produced the original figures
the_content_is_not_it.reading: Snatch is given six channels and its own objects, re-encoded, are given sixteen. The mid-file cut behaves the same way. Dredd, the accepted control, is sixteen both times. So the refusal is not about the object programme Snatch carries
the_content_is_not_it.the_re_encode_is_a_real_object_stream: not merely sixteen channels of something: oadec and Dolby agree on all fifteen active objects of the Snatch re-encode at 43,81 to 111,05 dB, correlation 0,99998 or better, with the sixteenth silent in both. That is ordinary configuration-0 agreement
the_content_is_not_it.what_it_leaves: the same question with one fewer answer. Not the configuration, not the sequence counter, not any field this decoder parses, and not the content. A property of how that stream was written, which no instrument here reaches
